title.narrative: Provision of community driven Food Security services to deliver solutions by ensuring the priorities of crisis-affected community in Jowhar

description.narrative: ltpgtAs of 2025, Somalia remains in a protracted humanitarian crisis shaped by the cumulative impacts of the 2020–2023 historic drought, recurrent flooding in late 2023 and mid-2024, and ongoing climatic volatility throughout 2025. These repeated shocks have continued to erode household coping capacities, particularly in rural and riverine areas where livelihoods depend heavily on seasonal agriculture and livestock. Despite short periods of recovery, many households have been unable to fully restore productive assets, leaving them highly exposed to further shocks.ltbrgtIn Jowhar District, conditions remain fragile at the close of 2025. Communities continue to face reduced agricultural output, loss of livestock, and constrained access to productive inputs, compounded by access challenges that limit timely humanitarian support. Fluctuations in the Shabelle River remain a persistent risk, with riverine and low-lying villages reporting repeated disruptions to cropping cycles and land usability. These pressures disproportionately affect rural households, internally displaced persons, women-headed households, and marginalized communities, increasing reliance on negative coping strategies and heightening the risk of further displacement if livelihoods are not stabilized.ltbrgtFindings from the community engagement (CE) process conducted in 2025 under the Area-Based Coordination (ABC) framework confirm that food insecurity and the inability to resume agricultural production remain the highest-ranked priorities for affected communities. Community members consistently identified lack of access to agricultural inputs, limited ability to prepare land for planting, and loss of livestock assets as the primary drivers of hunger. At the end of 2025, many households report insufficient food availability in both quantity and quality, particularly among displaced and riverine populations.ltbrgtIn response to these community-defined priorities, Wadajir Rural Development Organization (WARDO) proposes a community-driven Food Security and Livelihoods (FSL) intervention designed to stabilize food access and restore productive capacity during the critical transition from late 2025 into 2026. The project will support crisis-affected agro-pastoral households through the provision of agricultural input packages (fertilizers, seeds, pesticides and tools), tractor-based land preparation services, and targeted restocking of small livestock (shoats) in Micituure, reflecting both community prioritization and WARDO’s comparative advantage.ltbrgtAll activities will integrate protection mainstreaming, Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP), and PSEA safeguards to ensure assistance is safe, inclusive, and dignified, with particular attention to women, persons with disabilities, and marginalized groups. Anchored in 2025 community engagement outcomes and coordinated through ABC structures, the project aims to prevent further livelihood erosion, reduce displacement risks, and strengthen household resilience, enabling communities in Jowhar to enter 2026 with improved food security and restored livelihood foundations.ltbrgtlt/pgt
